div.div: Potential evidence completeness for High-relevance mapped datamodels — recommended CIM fields present in scope, not compliance scores.

div.p: What this shows: High-relevance controls per framework, stacked by how complete the mapped datamodel’s recommended CIM fields are in the selected sample.
Why it matters: Most controls point at a primary datamodel (for example Authentication). Recommended fields are the minimum set that datamodel expects to be useful.
Read it as: Good = ≥70% of recommended fields present; Partial = some; None = none. Potential evidence gaps only, not compliance. Open Governance IN for average completeness % and control detail.

search.query: | chart count over framework by evidence_band | fillnull value=0 Good Partial None | table framework Good Partial None | sort framework

div.p: What this shows: All High-relevance primary controls in scope, grouped by recommended-field completeness band (Good / Partial / None).
Why it matters: Shows how much of the primary governance map has a usable CIM field footprint versus partial or missing evidence.
Read it as: Potential evidence mix only — not compliance status or control effectiveness.

search.query: | stats count as controls by evidence_band | sort evidence_band

div.p: What this shows: Per-framework counts of High-relevance primary controls in each completeness band, plus average recommended-field %.
Why it matters: Connects the stacked gap view to control counts and a single completeness number for drill-down into Governance IN.
Read it as: Potential evidence summary only — not framework compliance or audit assurance.

search.query: | stats dc(control_reference) as mapped_controls dc(eval(if(evidence_band="Good",control_reference,null()))) as good_controls dc(eval(if(evidence_band="Partial",control_reference,null()))) as partial_controls dc(eval(if(evidence_band="None",control_reference,null()))) as none_controls avg(control_coverage_pct) as avg_coverage_pct dc(capability) as mapped_capabilities dc(primary_datamodel) as primary_datamodels by framework framework_version | eval avg_coverage_pct=round(avg_coverage_pct,1) | rename framework as Framework framework_version as Version mapped_controls as "Primary Controls" good_controls as Good partial_controls as Partial none_controls as None avg_coverage_pct as "Avg recommended %" mapped_capabilities as "Mapped Capabilities" primary_datamodels as "Primary Datamodels" | table Framework Version "Primary Controls" Good Partial None "Avg recommended %" "Mapped Capabilities" "Primary Datamodels" | sort - Good Framework

div.p: What this shows: How strongly each data source aligns with governance-mapped datamodels in the selected framework scope.
Why it matters: Source-level relevance helps show where the telemetry evidence behind governance coverage is coming from.
Read it as: This is a relevance indicator based on observed datamodel and governance mapping evidence. It does not mean the source is approved, compliant or required for retention.

search.query: | mvexpand datamodels | rename datamodels as datamodel | join type=left max=0 datamodel [ | inputlookup governance_datamodel_mapping_lookup | eval selected_framework=if(len("$framework_filter$")=0,"*","$framework_filter$") | eval selected_framework_wrapped="|" . selected_framework . "|" | where selected_framework="*" OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|*|%") OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|" . framework . "|%") | fields framework datamodel governance_relevance mapping_confidence retention_importance ] | eval governance_mapped=if(isnotnull(framework),1,0) | stats dc(field_name) as matched_dm_fields dc(datamodel) as matched_datamodel_count values(governance_relevance) as relevance_values values(mapping_confidence) as confidence_values values(retention_importance) as importance_values max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value | eval high_relevance=if(mvfind(relevance_values,"High")>=0 OR mvfind(relevance_values,"Medium-High")>=0,1,0) | eval high_confidence=if(mvfind(confidence_values,"High")>=0,1,0) | eval medium_confidence=if(mvfind(confidence_values,"Medium")>=0,1,0) | eval governance_relevance=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped", high_relevance=1 AND high_confidence=1 AND matched_datamodel_count>=2, "High", high_relevance=1 OR high_confidence=1, "Medium-High", medium_confidence=1, "Medium", true(), "Low" ) | stats count by governance_relevance

div.p: What this shows: A source-level tiering guidance indicator derived from matched governance mappings.
Why it matters: Tiering context can help frame discussions about searchability, archival value and governance evidence preservation.
Read it as: This is guidance from configured mappings, not a policy decision. Final tiering decisions should consider customer policy, operational use and regulatory requirements.

div.p: What this shows: Searchable-retention guidance derived from governance-mapped framework evidence.
Why it matters: Retention context helps identify where telemetry may have ongoing governance, audit or investigation value.
Read it as: This is not a retention policy or legal recommendation. It reflects configured governance mapping evidence within the selected scope.

"|" | where selected_framework="*" OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|*|%") OR like(selected_framework_wrapped,"%|" . framework . "|%") | fields framework datamodel searchable_retention_recommendation ] | eval governance_mapped=if(isnotnull(framework),1,0) | stats values(searchable_retention_recommendation) as searchable_values max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value | eval retention_category=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped / review", mvfind(searchable_values,"Long")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"long")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"summary")>=0, "Longer summary", mvfind(searchable_values,"Medium")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"medium")>=0, "Medium", mvfind(searchable_values,"Short")>=0 OR mvfind(searchable_values,"short")>=0, "Short-to-medium", true(), "Review" ) | stats count by retention_category

div.p: What this shows: A source-level evidence summary of framework mapping, datamodel coverage, retention guidance and tiering guidance.
Why it matters: Bringing these signals together helps explain why some telemetry appears more relevant to governance, audit or investigation conversations.

Read it as: This is an evidence summary, not a decision record. Unmapped rows may still contain useful datamodel evidence, but no governance mapping currently exists for those datamodels in the selected framework scope.

p.strong: This does not assert compliance. It highlights telemetry that appears relevant to selected governance drivers and shows where mapping is currently missing.

div.p: What this shows: Detailed framework-to-capability-to-datamodel mapping evidence behind the executive coverage and source-level governance indicators.
Why it matters: This panel exposes the rationale, confidence and field evidence used to support governance coverage calculations.
Read it as: Each row is supporting evidence for review and validation. It should be used to understand how DIG reached a result, not as a standalone compliance conclusion.

div.p: What this shows: The calculation model used to connect governance frameworks, control areas, DIG capabilities, Splunk datamodels and observed telemetry evidence.

Why it matters: Governance coverage should be explainable and defensible. This methodology explains how DIG turns configured mappings and observed datamodel evidence into framework coverage indicators.
Read it as: This dashboard shows telemetry alignment evidence. It supports governance and audit conversations but does not replace formal compliance assessment, control testing or policy review.
